claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are some specific rules that apply. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or doing A-levels or anything like that. He's not studying at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and not in approved education or training, I need to ask about his work situation, as this affects eligibility.

**Is Alex currently working? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a couple more questions to help determine your eligibility:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right?** (For example, Universal Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, or any other benefits?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or are you looking to make a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm looking to make a new claim - I haven't been claiming it before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. One final question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** (This can be relevant for 16-17 year olds who have left education or training)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure actually - I don't know if he's registered with any careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you would be ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

For children aged 16 and over, Child Benefit normally only continues if the child stays in **approved education or training**. Since Alex is 17 and is not currently in college, doing A-levels, or any other approved education or training, he doesn't meet this key requirement.

While there is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education, this applies to existing Child Benefit claims when circumstances change. Since you're looking to make a new claim now (and Alex has already left education), this provision wouldn't apply to your situation.

**What you might consider:**
- If Alex decides to return to education or approved training in the future, you could claim Child Benefit at that point
- You could encourage Alex to explore education or training opportunities, which would make him eligible again

If you have any questions about this decision or Alex's circumstances change, please feel free to ask!
